title: Eval Change Pulse: Console Dashboard + Alert Suppression Bridge
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Build a Console-first experience that surfaces sudden quality regressions caused by model or config changes and integrates with alerting endpoints (Slack + PagerDuty) while minimizing noise via an adaptive suppression layer (the 'suppression bridge'). This ticket scopes the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for a dashboard widget (Change Pulse) and the server-side orchestration needed to attach dedupe/suppression metadata to alert events. The feature should tie eval regression signals to specific model/config diffs (model version, quantization profile, routing policy, prompt template, batching parameters, and KV/cache settings) and provide remediation actions (rollback link, pin model, start canary).
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: A new Change Pulse panel exists in the Evals section showing recent eval score deltas by change hash with sortable columns (time, delta magnitude, affected metric, impacted traffic).
Attribution: Each alerted regression includes a causal diff: model_version, config_hash, and a human-readable description of the top-3 candidate changes.
Alerting: Console can send deduplicated alerts to Slack (channels + threads) and PagerDuty with consistent fingerprinting so repeat regressions within a cooldown window are suppressed or grouped.
Suppression Bridge: Configurable per-project suppression policy exists (cooldown window, grouping threshold, sticky dedupe by change-hash).
Operators: Runbook link + one-click rollback/pin action in the dashboard that opens the rollout management page with pre-filled context.
Telemetry: Events emitted include change_hash, eval_id, metric_delta, sample_size, and suppression_reason; metrics land in telemetry pipeline for monitoring and SLOs.
tasks: Product: Finalize UX copy and wireframes for Change Pulse (link to mock in links).
Design: High-fidelity mockups for desktop and mobile console views; include grouped regression view and action menu.
Engineering (Backend): Build change-attribution service that computes change_hash and candidate diffs for each eval run; expose API for console and alerting service.
Engineering (Alerting): Implement suppression bridge that consumes change-attribution output and applies adaptive cooldown windows; implement Slack + PagerDuty payload formats.
Engineering (Frontend): Implement dashboard widget, table, and drilldown details page; wire rollback/pin action to rollout APIs.
QA: Create integration tests that simulate model/config changes and ensure alerts are grouped and suppression works as configured.
Docs: Draft console docs describing policies, tuning guidance, and example webhook payloads.
Launch: Run a 2-week canary on 10% of orgs with heavy eval traffic, collect feedback, iterate.
discussions: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Khan: Kickoff notes: aligned with Evals Reliability OKR. Need to prioritize attribution fidelity vs runtime cost. Refer to ENG-20577 for telemetry baseline.
2025-02-18 - Liam Ortega: PM/Eng sync: Backend will compute change_hash using ordered serializable config diff; propose sampling mode for heavy eval workloads to reduce cost.
2025-02-24 - Naomi Park (Design): Delivered first mock (see links). Review requested: how to surface instability vs one-off noise.

2025-03-01 - Rahul Desai (Engineering): Implemented first pass suppression bridge prototype; found edge-case where small metric deltas from low-sample evals trigger alerts; proposed minimum sample-size threshold.
notes: Tradeoffs: Tight attribution improves signal but increases compute cost; will start with best-effort attribution + sample-size gating and iterate based on false-positive rate.
Open question: Whether alert grouping should be tenant-scoped or global (per-org recommended for now).
Fallback behavior: If attribution fails, alerts should still surface with 'unknown change' tag and link to raw eval snapshot for manual triage.
